      <title>LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</link>
      <description><p>At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports</p><p>Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a <a href="https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/12/senegal-brutal-crackdown-violates-lgbt-peoples-rights">new report</a>.</p><p>More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, <a href="https://www.hivjustice.net/cases/senegal-crackdown-on-lgbtq-people-intensifies-with-multiple-arrests/">according to HIV Justice Network</a>, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial</link>
      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Austerity is inevitably painful’: How Michael Gove justifies his politics | Radical Thinking with Aditya Chakrabortty – podcast</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/commentisfree/audio/2026/oct/17/austerity-is-inevitably-painful-how-michael-gove-justifies-his-politics-radical-thinking-with-aditya-chakrabortty-podcast</link>
      <description><p>For more than three decades, Michael Gove has been a leading figure in British Conservatism. As a journalist, government minister and now editor of the Tory bible, the Spectator, he has helped shape the right even as it has moved further rightwards. In the latest episode of Radical Thinking, Gove joins Aditya Chakrabortty to discuss the future of the right, his record on Brexit and austerity, and the Spectator’s position on Islam</p><p>Watch the full episode with Michael Gove <a href="https://youtu.be/cIGXagkUFr8">here</a>.
 <br>
 <br>
 Aditya’s suggested reading:</p><p>To read the fruits of Michael Gove’s dalliance with the Marxism Today gang, look up his essay in a 1998 collection called The Moderniser’s Dilemma: Radical Politics in the Age of Blair</p><p>For slalom ride through Michael Gove’s years in power, read <a href="https://www.lrb.co.uk/the-paper/v41/n17/richard-j.-evans/the-demented-dalek">The Demented Dalek</a> by the historian Richard J Evans in the London Review of Books</p><p>To learn more on what’s become of the British right, there’s a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2024/sep/12/tory-leadership-jenrick-tugendhat-cleverly-badenoch">column by me </a>for the Guardian</p><p>Just why the most successful political party is now failing is analysed in-depth by Phil Burton-Cartledge in his book <a href="https://guardianbookshop.com/the-partys-over-9781839760372/">The Party’s Over: The Rise and Fall of the Conservatives from Thatcher to Sunak</a></p><p>Phil also writes a very good blog on British politics, which keeps a close eye on how each party is trying to marshall a coalition of voters. <a href="https://averypublicsociologist.blogspot.com/2026/10/the-clear-blue-water-strategy.html">Here</a> he is on Kemi Badenoch</p><p>Geoffrey Wheatcroft does an entertaining short narrative in <a href="https://guardianbookshop.com/bloody-panico-9781804295755/">Bloody Panico!:</a></p><p><a href="https://guardianbookshop.com/bloody-panico-9781804295755/">or, Whatever Happened to The Tory Party</a></p><p>For more on the economics of the Cameron years, <a href="https://foundationaleconomy.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/01/wp87.pdf">this paper</a> is acute on how the Tories failed to move the UK away from being a country of renters towards a country of makers. Two of its authors will join us for a podcast later in the series.</p><p>And if you want to read how Brexit may have cost the UK 8% of GDP, there’s <a href="https://www.nber.org/papers/w34459?st_source=ai_overview">this paper</a> based on data from the Bank of England</p><p>Finally, on the Spectator read Nesrine Malik’s recent column in The Guardian</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/jul/20/islamophobia-spectator-britain-oldest-political-magazine">Why has Britain’s oldest political magazine become such a rabid cheerleader for Islamophobia?</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/commentisfree/audio/2026/oct/17/austerity-is-inevitably-painful-how-michael-gove-justifies-his-politics-radical-thinking-with-aditya-chakrabortty-podcast">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal</p><p>Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding.       <description><p>As Mark Cocker approaches a landmark for the world’s oldest column in an English-language newspaper, he is still inspired by powerful encounters with nature</p><p>In the autumn of 1987, Mark Cocker sat in a field near Norwich and watched a jay burying acorns for the long winter ahead.       <description><p>Environmental watchdog Mighty Earth reveals two-year effort to postpone and weaken EU Deforestation Regulation</p><p>US corporate lobbyists launched a two-year “blitz” to postpone and weaken the world’s most progressive legislation to protect forests, according to a new investigation by the environmental watchdog Mighty Earth.</p><p>Major US firms and trade associations, including Cargill, Bunge, Mondelēz and the US Soybean Export Council, as well as numerous other US firms and organizations, sought to influence the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) in more than 350 meetings, the advocacy group <a href="http://mightyearth.org/knives-out-eudr">found</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/17/us-corporate-lobbyists-europe-deforestation">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Key player in false Talarico rumor has history of online posts invoking Nazi Germany</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/17/talarico-mental-health-facility-rumor-ryan-amacher</link>
      <description><p>Ryan Amacher, who played role in bid to damage campaign, has also made antisemitic and racist posts on social media</p><p>An influencer who played a key role in <a href="https://apnews.com/article/fact-check-talarico-mental-health-lindner-634591c8818aeab31c52526032d0387c">hoax claims</a> that James Talarico was in a mental health facility has a long history of social media posts that <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2078194489852895256">favorably invoke Nazi Germany</a>, express <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2007075498573304201">antisemitism</a> and <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/1937249007476375763">anti-Black racism</a>, <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2107868676200546531">criticize miscegenation</a> and call for <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2016267517459890302">“remigration”</a> of refugees.</p><p>On X, the <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/1944951540391010351">Lake Oswego, Oregon, resident</a> Ryan Amacher, known online as Rhein Amacher, has described Muslims as <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2070784307011223569">“sub-human”</a>, claimed that Black Africans are <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2068263824004968725">“monkeys” with low IQ</a>, characterized immigrants as <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2071389790860382648">“vermin”</a> and expressed support for the far right, including <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/2049960060894486905">Germany’s AfD</a> and the UK’s <a href="https://x.com/RheinAmacher/status/1929199466055360629">Tommy Robinson</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/17/talarico-mental-health-facility-rumor-ryan-amacher">Continue reading...</a></description>
